newsitem.title: USA: Former MGM head sought after apparent U.S. flight.
newsitem.headline: Former MGM head sought after apparent U.S. flight.

text.p: An arrest warrant was issued on Friday for the former chief of the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer movie studio after the Italian financier apparently fled the United States to avoid a court sentence.

The flamboyant financier, Giancarlo Parretti, was due to be sentenced on Monday in a Delaware court after being found guilty last October on charges of evidence tampering and perjury, which carry a sentence of up to 10 years.
But his attorneys said they had received word by fax on Friday that Parretti was in Italy. "It seems as if he is gone," Wilmington attorney Eugene Maurer told Reuters.
Maurer said he had received a fax from an Italian lawyer saying he was acting on Parretti's behalf.
Attorney Jay Coggan, in Los Angeles, said he had heard from Parretti directly. "It (the fax) said effectively nothing more than the fact that he was in Italy," Coggan said.
"I was personally surprised that it occurred. I've always know him to be an honourable man and I found this uncharacteristic," Coggan said.

Parretti, who began as as a hotel waiter in Italy, had charmed his way to an opulent lifestyle and control over one of Hollywood's most prestigious studios, before being ousted in 1991 by the French bank, Credit Lyonnais, whose subsidiary had lent him the money to buy MGM.
Parretti was indicted in 1992 on charges he altered documents and lied about it in a 1991 Delaware civil trial over his ouster.
He had returned voluntarily from Italy to face trial and has been free on bail and living in California. Attorneys said Parretti stands to forfeit bonds in Delaware and California totalling $125,000.
Furthermore, Coggan said, a $3.9 billion lawsuit filed by Parretti against Credit Lyonnais over the ouster would probably be thrown out as a result of the flight.
"I think the man will probably remain free in Italy and I think his lawsuit in Los Angeles will be thrown out and he will not be able to return to the U.S.," he said.
A U.S. Attorney's spokesman in California said criminal bail-jumping charges against Parretti would be considered if his flight from the United States was confirmed.
Parretti also is wanted in France on charges of fraud, theft and embezzlement in connection with the MGM deal.
Maurer said the fax he received came from a lawyer named Manlio Morcella in Orvieto, Italy. That is the town, about 50 miles (80 km) north of Rome, where Parretti was raised on an olive farm.
Coggan said he had tried to contact Parretti but had not spoken with him since receiving the fax.
Maurer said Delaware Superior Court Judge Richard Cooch issued the warrant and cancelled Monday's sentencing after a meeting on Friday with Maurer and state prosecutor Paul Wallace.
Wallace could not be reached for comment.

Parretti bought MGM in 1991 for $1.3 billion from financier Kirk Kerkorian, who returned to the studio in July 1996 as part of a management-led buyout from a French state-owned holding company formed to dispose of assets of the troubled Credit Lyonnais.
